NEXT-SHAPE fleet config (ADR-0031: runner pool and job queue; ADR-0032: scheduling policy from
run history). This file is NOT read by the running supervisor: the code that understands it
ships alongside, and a supervisor started before that code keeps its last good config and
complains if it sees this shape. At the next drain window the operator renames this file over
fleet.json and restarts the fleet service (docs/OPERATIONS.md, 'Switching to the pool/queue
shape'). The new code also loads the OLD shape, so either file works after the restart.
accounts.pinned: account -> lane name. A pinned lane is exactly today's lane: one lane, one
account, its own roster stream, enabled/drain/respawn semantics unchanged. The lanes list
holds ONLY pinned lanes; every lane there must appear in accounts.pinned.
accounts.pool: the accounts the policy and the queue may use, in preference order. Never
PROBE, never SMOKE*.
roster: named entries, the exact per-entry schema of roster JSONs. No entry carries an
account: the pool assigns one. Two optional scheduling fields (ADR-0032):
tiers: a manual FORCE — tiers listed here are eligible regardless of run history. Normally
absent: every model is e90-eligible on arrival and e360 is EARNED (one un-overridden
e90 run that reached level 5). Use it to push a model into e360 by hand.
runsPerEpisode: { e90: n, e360: n } overrides policy.runsPerEpisode for this entry.
policy: runsPerEpisode targets (default 3 and 3). Everything else about the policy is code:
a stillborn run (zero model responses) never counts toward a target but climbs the defer
ladder; the ladder is 1m/3m/5m/10m/15m/30m/1h/3h/6h on consecutive no-progress attempts
(stillborn or adapter-error) and one more failure at the 6h ceiling RETIRES the model until
`infra/run-fleet.sh --clear-model <name>`. Priority for a free pool account: models with no
counted run yet, then e90 before e360, then fewest counted runs, ties by roster order. One
stream per model. --status shows every model's verdict; --dry-run shows the next picks.
queue: ordered MANUAL jobs { ref, episode, repeat, lane?, enabled? }; they outrank the policy,
which only fills accounts the queue leaves free. `ref` is a roster name or a list of them (a
list rotates several models on one account as a multi-entry lane does). `episode` is
e90 | e360 | freeplay (freeplay is never scheduled by the policy; it is only reachable here).
`repeat` is a count or "loop" (run-roster --loop; a loop job holds its account until disabled).
`lane` names the job's run ids and logs (fleet-<lane>-<model>-<stamp>); default <first
ref>-<episode>. A job whose episode a ref is not eligible for runs without that ref; a job
with no eligible ref is SKIPPED with a logged reason. Example entries (the queue below is
empty on purpose — the policy runs the roster):
{ "ref": "sonnet", "episode": "e360", "repeat": 1, "lane": "sonnet-e360" }
{ "ref": ["hy3", "deepseek-flash"], "episode": "e90", "repeat": "loop", "lane": "free-oc-a", "enabled": false }
Lane policy is unchanged and enforced on every entry: claude models only via the
claude-subscription driver; shared free pools carry free ids only; a local apiBase is
exempt from the suffix rule. preflight is unchanged (ADR-0023); its accounts may not be
in the pool.
